concerns.text: FR-009/FR-012 and the spec's Execution Metric entity require `precision_at_10`, and plan Phase 2-d says 'Record latency, translation_error, timeout_flag, success_flag, precision_at_10 (FR-009)'. But neither execution_log.schema.yaml, execution_metric.schema.yaml, nor the data-model 'Execution Metric' entity defines a `precision_at_10` field, and the CSV column list in data-model.md omits it. The plan references a field the data model does not define; SC-002 (Precision@10 difference ≤ 0.02) cannot be computed from the contracted artifacts.

Two near-duplicate contracts exist: `statistics-result.schema.yaml` (hyphen) and `statistics_result.schema.yaml` (underscore). Plan/data-model reference only the underscore version; the hyphen version is an orphan duplicate that creates SSoT ambiguity (Constitution Principle I). Delete one and reference the survivor consistently.

Phase 2-a produces `baseline_overhead.json`, but this artifact appears in neither the data-model entities/file formats nor the plan's Project Structure tree. Every persistent artifact should be defined once in the data model (Principle IV traceability).

Plan and research use `corrected_latency_ms` as the ANOVA dependent variable, but the schema/data-model field is `latency_ms` (described as baseline-corrected). Pick one name so the stats module's input column matches the contract.

SC-001 requires the slope-ratio (graph vs. text, > 1.5) via simple linear regression on mean latency per depth, but Phase 3's deliverables and `anova_results.json` structure contain no slope-ratio computation or field. Add it to Phase 3 and the statistics output contract so SC-001 is checkable.

FR-001 mandates 'a strict CPU time limit per query of ≤ 1,000 ms' enforced via cgroups; the plan only mentions a generic 'cgroups CPU quota' and the 60 s timeout. The plan should state the ≤ 1000 ms CPU quota explicitly (or note the deviation) so implementation matches the spec.
